label: SFP28 25GBASE-ER 40 km
notes: 25GBASE-ER per IEEE 802.3cc (Clause 114), Tables 114-6 and 114-7: average launch power -3.0..+6.0 dBm in the 1295-1310 nm lane window, average receive power -21.0 (min) to -4.0 (max) dBm, receiver sensitivity in OMA -19.0 dBm, stressed receiver sensitivity in OMA -16.5 dBm, 40 km over G.652. The class's own channel insertion loss is 18 dB, which is exactly -3.0 minus -21.0 - the same min-launch-to-min-receive convention as the 10GBASE, 25GBASE-LR and 100GBASE-LR4 rows, and the figure the engine recomputes for a link of this pair (measured: budgetDb 18). Do not read 20.7 dB off a vendor sheet as the budget: that is the 18 dB channel plus the 2.7 dB transmitter-and-dispersion penalty the standard also allows, and the engine already spends the whole 18 dB. Corroboration from shipped modules: Cisco SFP-25G-ER-I prints +6.0/-3.0 dBm transmit and -4.0/-21.0 dBm receive over 1295-1310 nm for 40 km, and Alpha Bridge ASFP28-25G-ER prints the same -3/+6 and -21/-4. Sheet-to-sheet spread is real - 6COM's 6C-SFP28-ER quotes 0..+6 dBm launch and -23..-5 dBm receive, a tighter transmitter and a looser receiver than the class - so this row is the class, not one vendor's module. 40 km is quoted at the clause's RS(528,514) FEC on every sheet ('40 km with FEC'); a host that does not enable FEC is not this row. Two consequences worth seeing before a build. First, reach is the binding limit, not loss: at 0.35 dB/km 40 km x 0.35 = 14.0 dB of fibre plus the engine's default two SC/APC matings at 0.3 dB each = 14.6 dB ODN (measured), leaving 3.4 dB of headroom, so a full-reach 40 km link reads marginal at the default 3 dB margin - the engine calls a link ok only from 5 dB of headroom, which ends at 35.4 km ((18 - 0.6 - 5) / 0.35), and 41.1 km would still sit inside the loss budget but is outside the 40 km reach and is refused by name. Second, the class assumes at least 10 dB of span loss (6.0 minus -4.0), i.e. about 28.6 km of G.652.D at 0.35 dB/km, so a shorter span can overdrive the far end and needs a pad rather than more reach. The engine budgets at the minimum launch, so a bare patch reads -3.6 dBm against -4.0 and its attenuator verdict asks for a 1 dB pad (measured); at the +6.0 dBm ceiling the same 10 km span asks for 6 dB (measured), so re-budget a short span at txDbm: 6 rather than trusting the minimum-launch pad. One limit this row inherits from the model rather than the standard: it is recorded at 1310 nm, the same single wavelength as the 25GBASE-LR row, so budget.pointToPoint cannot tell the two classes apart and does not refuse a mixed pair (measured: an ER head end into an LR customer end is accepted). Pair ER with ER - a shipped ER module is not qualified against an LR receiver - and note that a mixed pair is held to the shorter optic's 10 km reach, which is what catches a 40 km span (measured: that link fails on reach, on headroom and on the LR row's 10.3 dB budget). Class figures from the recommendation, not one measured module: replace the row with the module actually purchased before pricing a build.
